title: Register and sign in with a hashed, non-logged credential
business_value: A member can create an account and prove identity on later visits, which every other capability (create, list, delete) requires as its entry gate.
user_story: As a visitor, I want to register with an email and password and then sign in, so that I receive a session I can use to manage my links.
description: POST /auth/register and POST /auth/sign-in issue an HTTP-only session cookie on success. Passwords are hashed with Argon2id before storage and never appear, plaintext or hashed, in any log line the app writes for these two requests.
scope_in: Register with email + password
Sign in with email + password, receiving an HTTP-only session cookie
Argon2id password hashing at rest
Excluding password/hash bytes from all log output for register and sign-in requests
scope_out: Password reset by email, SSO, or multi-factor authentication (SG-7)

acceptance_criteria.given: a registered email and correct password
acceptance_criteria.then: the response sets an HTTP-only session cookie and a subsequent authenticated request succeeds

acceptance_criteria.given: a member registering with a new email and password
acceptance_criteria.when: the stored credential is read back
acceptance_criteria.then: it begins with `$argon2id$`

acceptance_criteria.given: a member registering and then signing in
acceptance_criteria.when: the application's full log output for those two requests is scanned
acceptance_criteria.then: it contains neither the plaintext password nor the stored hash

acceptance_criteria.given: an unregistered email or a wrong password
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 401 and no session cookie is set

title: Sign out invalidates the session server-side
business_value: A member can end their session on a shared or public machine with confidence the old cookie stops working, not just that the browser forgets it.
user_story: As a signed-in member, I want to sign out, so that the session cookie I used can no longer authenticate requests.
description: POST /auth/sign-out deletes the server-side session record so the previously issued cookie is rejected on the next authenticated request, distinct from a purely client-side cookie clear.
scope_in: Server-side session invalidation on sign-out
401 on any authenticated request replaying the invalidated cookie

depends_on.reason: sign-out invalidates the session E1-S1 creates at sign-in

acceptance_criteria.then: a subsequent authenticated request returns 401

acceptance_criteria.given: a signed-in member who has just signed out
acceptance_criteria.when: the same session cookie from before sign-out is replayed
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is rejected with 401 rather than succeeding, because the session was invalidated server-side and not merely cleared client-side

acceptance_criteria.given: a request with no active session
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 401 and no server state changes

title: Create a short link with an SSRF-safe target and a cryptographically random code
business_value: A signed-in member can turn a long URL into a short, shareable code, while the service refuses targets that would let the redirect be weaponized against internal infrastructure.
user_story: As a signed-in member, I want to submit a target URL and receive a short code, so that I can share a compact link that still points at a safe, public destination.
description: POST /links validates the target's scheme and host literally (no DNS lookup, no outbound fetch), rejects unsafe targets with 422, and otherwise mints a code of at least 7 characters drawn from a CSPRNG with at least 40 bits of entropy.
scope_in: POST /links for a signed-in member
Scheme allow-list: http, https only
Host deny-list: PUBLIC_BASE_URL, localhost, and private/loopback/link-local/unique-local/cloud-metadata IP literals
Literal string/IP-range host inspection only — no DNS resolution, no outbound fetch
Code generation via secrets/os.urandom, >=7 chars, >=40 bits entropy, collision-free
scope_out: Editing a link's target after creation (SG-2)
Following redirect chains or resolving hostnames to validate them (SG-10)

depends_on.reason: create requires a signed-in session established by E1-S1

acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 201 with a code of at least 7 characters

the response is 422; the same holds for a host matching PUBLIC_BASE_URL and for each of `http://192.168.1.1/`, `http://10.0.0.1/`, `http://127.0.0.1/`, `http://[::1]/`, `http://169.254.169.254/` and `http://localhost/`

acceptance_criteria.when: a target URL is inspected during creation
acceptance_criteria.then: only literal scheme/host/IP-range checks run — no DNS lookup and no outbound network fetch occurs
every code is at least 7 characters drawn from a 62-character alphanumeric alphabet (>= 41.7 bits), no two are equal, and the bytes come from `secrets`/`os.urandom` rather than the `random` module

acceptance_criteria.given: a request with no valid session
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 401 and no link row is created

title: Redirect a known code to its target
business_value: The short code a member shares actually takes the recipient to the intended destination, which is the core value the whole product delivers.
user_story: As anyone holding a short code, I want to open it and land on the target URL, so that the short link works like the long URL it replaced.
description: GET /{code} looks up the code and, when it exists and is not deleted, returns HTTP 302 with Location set to the stored target. The handler never fetches the target itself.
scope_in: GET /{code} for an existing, not-deleted code returns 302 with Location
GET /{code} for a code that was never issued returns 404
scope_out: Redirect for a deleted code (owned by E5-S1's delete acceptance)
Click counts or analytics on redirect (SG-4)

depends_on.reason: redirect needs an existing link row created by E2-S1

acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 302 with `Location` set to the target URL

acceptance_criteria.given: a code that was never issued
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 404

acceptance_criteria.when: it resolves a code to a target URL
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns the Location header to the caller without itself following or fetching the target URL

title: List the signed-in member's own links
business_value: A member can see everything they have shortened in one place, newest first, without ever seeing another member's data.
user_story: As a signed-in member, I want to see my own links on a console page, newest first and paginated, so that I can find and manage what I have created.
description: GET /links returns the signed-in member's own links, newest first, 20 per page, and the console page renders that list. No other member's links are ever included.
scope_in: GET /links with pagination (20 per page), newest first, scoped to the caller
Console list page rendering the returned links
Empty-state rendering when the member owns zero links
scope_out: Editing a link from the list (SG-2)
Click counts, analytics, or export from the list (SG-4, SG-9)

depends_on.reason: list requires a signed-in session established by E1-S1
list requires existing links created by E2-S1

acceptance_criteria.then: exactly 20 links are returned, newest first, and none belongs to another user
the remaining 5 links are returned, newest-first order preserved across the page boundary
the page renders an empty state with no links and no error

acceptance_criteria.given: two members who each own links
acceptance_criteria.when: the second member requests the list endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: only the second member's own links appear — never the first member's

title: Create and list responses stay under a 300ms p95 at 100 links
business_value: The console and create flow stay responsive as a member accumulates links, instead of degrading as their list grows.
user_story: As a signed-in member with many links, I want create and list to stay fast, so that managing a large set of links does not feel slow.
description: A load-test harness seeds 100 links for one account via the create endpoint, then samples repeated create and list calls, asserting p95 latency under 300ms for each and emitting a machine-readable report for the evaluator.
scope_in: Load-test harness seeding 100 links via POST /links
p95 latency measurement for POST /links and GET /links
Machine-readable timing report consumable by /evaluate

depends_on.reason: measures the list endpoint E4-S1 implements
seeds the 100 links and measures the create endpoint E2-S1 implements

acceptance_criteria.then: the p95 response time across the sample is under 300 ms

acceptance_criteria.when: calling the list endpoint for page 1 repeatedly
acceptance_criteria.then: the p95 response time across the sample is under 300 ms

acceptance_criteria.when: it seeds 100 links and samples both endpoints in one run
acceptance_criteria.then: it writes a single machine-readable report recording both p95 figures for the evaluator to check

title: Console list page meets WCAG 2.2 AA
business_value: Members using assistive technology can operate the console as fully as any other member.
user_story: As a member using assistive technology, I want the console list page to be accessible, so that I can view and manage my links without a mouse or with a screen reader.
description: The console list page (rendered by E4-S1) is scanned with an automated WCAG 2.2 AA checker, is fully keyboard-operable, and meets minimum color-contrast requirements.
scope_in: Automated WCAG 2.2 AA scan of the console list page
Full keyboard operability of pagination and per-link actions
Minimum color-contrast compliance
scope_out: Accessibility of pages outside the console list (sign-in/register forms are covered only if reused by this page)

depends_on.reason: scans and audits the page E4-S1 renders

acceptance_criteria.when: it is scanned with an automated WCAG 2.2 AA checker (e.g. axe)
acceptance_criteria.then: zero level-A or level-AA violations are reported

acceptance_criteria.when: operated with keyboard only, no mouse
acceptance_criteria.then: every interactive element (pagination, delete action) is reachable and operable in a visible focus order

acceptance_criteria.when: its text and interactive elements are measured for contrast
acceptance_criteria.then: every element meets the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum contrast ratio

title: Delete a member's own link
business_value: A member can revoke a link they no longer want live, and be certain nobody else can reuse the freed-up code.
user_story: As a signed-in member, I want to delete one of my own links, so that its code stops working and I control what stays shareable.
description: DELETE /links/{code} removes the member's own link, returns 204, makes later requests for that code 404, and never reissues the freed code to a new link.
scope_in: DELETE /links/{code} for the owning member returns 204
Deleted code returns 404 on later redirect
Deleted code is never reissued to a new link
Deleting another member's link is rejected

depends_on.reason: delete requires a signed-in session established by E1-S1
delete requires an existing link row created by E2-S1

acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 204

acceptance_criteria.given: a member's own link that was just deleted
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 404
the deleted code is never reissued to the new link

acceptance_criteria.given: a link owned by another member
acceptance_criteria.when: the signed-in member attempts to delete it
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 404, not 204, and the other member's link is unaffected

title: Expose /healthz reflecting database reachability
business_value: Operators and orchestrators can tell whether the service is actually able to serve traffic, not just whether the process is running.
user_story: As an operator, I want a health endpoint that reflects database reachability, so that I can detect and react to a database outage automatically.
description: GET /healthz requires no authentication, checks database reachability, and returns 200 when reachable or 503 when not, with a small JSON body describing status.
scope_in: GET /healthz, unauthenticated
200 when the database is reachable
503 when the database is unreachable
scope_out: Structured request logging as a deliverable (SG-11)

acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 200
the response is 503
no authentication was required and the body is JSON describing database status

title: Return a safe 503 JSON envelope when the database is unreachable
business_value: When the database goes down, callers of any endpoint get a clean, predictable error instead of a leaking stack trace or a hang.
user_story: As an API caller, I want a clean 503 JSON error when the database is unreachable, so that my client can handle the outage without seeing internal details.
description: A shared database-reachability check (reused from E6-S1) backs a global error handler: when the database is unreachable, every endpoint other than /healthz returns 503 with a JSON body carrying an `error` field and no stack trace, exception class name, or filesystem path.
scope_in: Global 503 JSON error envelope for DB-unreachable failures on all endpoints except /healthz
No stack trace, exception class name, or filesystem path in the response body
Recovery to normal status once the database is reachable again
scope_out: Structured request logging as a deliverable (SG-11)

depends_on.reason: reuses the database-reachability check E6-S1 implements for /healthz

acceptance_criteria.when: any API endpoint other than `/healthz` is called
acceptance_criteria.then: the response is 503 with a JSON body carrying an `error` field
it contains no stack trace, exception class name, or filesystem path
the response returns to its normal, non-503 status

title: Run the whole stack from one docker compose up
business_value: Anyone can stand up the entire system from a clean checkout with a single command and no external dependencies, which underpins every other story's ability to be demoed and evaluated.
user_story: As a developer or evaluator, I want `docker compose up` to bring up the whole stack, so that I can run and test the service without any manual setup or third-party network calls.
description: A docker-compose.yml brings up the API, web console, and a single Postgres 16 container, reaching healthy from a clean checkout with no image cache, and making no network call to any host outside the compose network at build or run time.
scope_in: docker-compose.yml with API, web, and exactly one Postgres 16 service
Healthy stack from `docker compose up` on a clean checkout
No outbound network calls at build or run time
scope_out: OpenAPI publication, scheduled purge jobs, and structured request logs as required deliverables (SG-11)

acceptance_criteria.given: a clean checkout with no project images cached
acceptance_criteria.then: the stack reaches healthy with exactly one Postgres 16 container

acceptance_criteria.when: build and runtime network traffic is inspected
acceptance_criteria.then: no service makes a request to a host outside the compose network
it defines exactly one Postgres 16 service and no other third-party managed service
